article.dek: Sunday's two card legs both land, Lamar Jackson's return lasts one snap, and Monday night in Seattle is the last game standing — with a reshuffled Seahawks line in front of it.

items.headline: Lead: Sunday's card legs both land — two games left on the Week 8 slate
paragraphs: Both of Sunday's card legs landed. The Los Angeles Rams beat the Chargers 24-9, so the morning's Hit Rate moneyline leg won. Denver beat Kansas City 28-24 outright, scoring 15 unanswered fourth-quarter points after trailing 24-13, so the morning's Value leg, Denver +1.5, won too.

What is left: Philadelphia at Washington kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET tonight, and Chicago at Seattle closes Week 8 on Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET. The evening board's one remaining card is on that Monday game — see below.
One note on the results above: settlement in the app is manual. These are the reported final scores, not an app settlement — log your own results honestly, winners and losers alike.
items.takeaway: Rams 24-9 and Broncos 28-24 mean both Sunday card legs landed — only Sunday night and Monday night remain.

items.headline: Injury roundup: Jackson's return lasts one snap; Sunday night inactives set; Seattle's line reshuffles
paragraphs: Baltimore's day turned fast. Lamar Jackson, cleared to return after missing three games with a high ankle sprain, suffered a right thumb injury on Baltimore's first offensive play at Buffalo and was ruled out. Backup Tyler Huntley then suffered a toe injury and was questionable to return, forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his NFL debut. Buffalo won 36-10. Baltimore now has a short week before hosting Jacksonville on Thursday night, and there is no Thursday starting-quarterback news yet — that is the injury story to watch this week, not something to guess at tonight.

For Sunday night, the inactive lists are set. Washington is without defensive tackles Daron Payne (foot) and Javon Kinlaw, while receiver Treylon Burks (foot) and tight end John Bates (shoulder) are both active. Philadelphia is without receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for a second straight game, plus linebacker Jihaad Campbell, cornerback Jonathan Jones and receiver Britain Covey; Saquon Barkley is active and expected to play on a pitch count, and cornerback Jakorian Bennett is not among the inactives.

For Monday night, Seattle's offensive line gets reshuffled. Starting left tackle Charles Cross is out with an ankle injury, so Josh Jones steps in at left tackle, newly acquired Quenton Nelson debuts at left guard, and Grey Zabel shifts to right guard. Chicago is without running back Kyle Monangai (toe) for a fourth straight game, Seattle is without receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee), linebacker Uchenna Nwosu is doubtful (ankle), and Chicago's D'Marco Jackson (ankle) and Malik Muhammad (toe) are questionable.
items.takeaway: Jackson out after one snap with a thumb injury, Huntley hurt too, and Baltimore faces a short week; Sunday night's inactives are set; Seattle's line reshuffles for Monday.

items.headline: Weather: cloudy and cool for Monday night in Seattle
paragraphs: Monday night in Seattle looks cloudy, with a high of 54 degrees during the day and temperatures falling toward the high 40s at night. The rain chance at night is about 10 percent, with a light east-northeast wind.
That is the forecast as it stands Sunday evening, reported as fact. It is not a reason to bet a total one way or the other.
items.takeaway: Seattle Monday night: cloudy, low 50s at kickoff falling toward the high 40s, about a 10 percent rain chance, light wind.

items.headline: Evening cards: Seattle moneyline is the new Hit Rate, Chicago +3 holds as Balanced, Value has no play
paragraphs: Hit Rate is now the Seattle moneyline at -166 at DraftKings, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET against Chicago, with a model probability of 0.561 and a play-through price of -171. Hit Rate is the pick the app rates most likely to win. Remember the app's own tutorial: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

Balanced is unchanged: Chicago +3 at -102 at FanDuel, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET at Seattle, with a model probability of 0.506 and a play-through price of -105. It is a strong pick without paying too much — the middle ground, and a good starting point for a new bettor.

Value has no play tonight. The app reports no offer currently satisfies the Value lane contract, so there is no Value pick on the evening board. Value is always the model's +EV play — when nothing qualifies, the app says so instead of forcing one.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate: Seattle moneyline -166. Balanced: Chicago +3 -102 at FanDuel. Value: no play tonight.

items.headline: A card that changes still means checking your own price
paragraphs: The cards above are priced at DraftKings and FanDuel. If your book is neither, the card price is not your price.

Tap Check in the app, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

Odds are price mechanics: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and staking setting — that part is deliberately conservative, and it lives in the app, not here.
items.takeaway: Your book's price is the one that matters — run it through Check and let that verdict decide.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Learn the Game: key numbers
paragraphs: A key number is a margin of victory that comes up more often than others. In the NFL, 3 is the biggest one, because so many games are decided by a field goal. That is why the difference between getting +3 and getting +2.5 matters more than it looks.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say you bet a team at +3, and they lose by exactly 3 points. That bet pushes — your stake comes back. The same bet at +2.5 loses, because the team did not cover 2.5. Same team, same game, same final score — a different number, a different result.
That is the lesson to carry into the app: when you run a spread through Check, the number itself is part of the bet, not just the price next to it.
items.takeaway: Three is football's biggest key number — at +3, a three-point loss pushes, while at +2.5 the same loss loses.

items.headline: Morning board vs evening board: Hit Rate replaced, Balanced unchanged, Value gone
paragraphs: The evening board replaces Hit Rate. The Rams moneyline at -258 at DraftKings is off the board because that game is final — Seattle moneyline at -166 at DraftKings takes its place, with a play-through price of -171. That is a recommendation replacement, not a price move on the same pick.
Balanced does not move at all: Chicago +3 stays at -102 at FanDuel, with the play-through price still -105. Same pick, same price as the morning board.

Value is gone for tonight. Denver +1.5 at -112 at FanDuel settled as an outright 28-24 win, and no new offer satisfies the Value contract on the evening board, so the lane sits empty rather than forcing a pick.
The evening refresh caught all of it. If your book shows something different from the prices above, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and let the app re-evaluate it for you.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate flips from the Rams to Seattle moneyline, Balanced holds Chicago +3 -102, and Value sits empty after Denver's win.

items.headline: Monday game? Monday check.
paragraphs: There is one piece of information worth waiting for: Monday night's inactive lists, about 90 minutes before kickoff, for the questionable names above. That is a real pending event with a set time.
Everything else is ready now. If your book has a good number on Chicago +3 and Check says bet, bet now — waiting for the Monday rush lets the number drift the wrong way too.

And a habit to keep from Sunday: settlement in the app is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log the losers too. A tracker that only holds winners is not a record, it is a highlight reel.
items.takeaway: Wait only for Monday night's inactive lists; otherwise bet when Check says bet — and log every result, winners and losers alike.
